title: The Commandments and Promises of Jesus Christ in the Gospels
theme: Discipleship through the teachings of Jesus
description: A discipleship-focused content pack built around the commandments, promises, invitations, and warnings of Jesus in the Gospels.

units.title: Repent and Believe the Good News
units.summary: Jesus opens his ministry by calling people to repentance and faith because the kingdom of God has drawn near.

passages.text: Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God's Kingdom, and saying, "The time is fulfilled, and God's Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News."

focus.statement: Repent, and believe in the Good News.

contextCard.title: The kingdom call
contextCard.body: Jesus does not begin with vague inspiration. He announces that God's kingdom is near and calls for a real response: turn from sin and trust the good news.

questions.prompt: What two responses does Jesus command in Mark 1:15?
questions.explanation: Jesus calls people to repentance and faith as the right response to the kingdom.

questions.prompt: Jesus says the kingdom is far away and not yet relevant.
questions.explanation: He says the kingdom of God is at hand.

questions.prompt: The time is fulfilled, and God's Kingdom is at hand! _____, and believe in the Good News.
questions.explanation: Repentance is part of Jesus' opening command.

reflection.prompt: Where is Jesus calling you to turn and trust him rather than delay obedience?

mission.intro: The call of the kingdom comes first. Advance by answering with repentance and faith.
mission.victoryText: You moved forward by receiving the kingdom call, not ignoring it.

units.title: Follow Me
units.summary: Jesus calls disciples not merely to admire him, but to follow him personally and leave old priorities behind.

passages.text: He said to them, "Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men." They immediately left their nets, and followed him.
If anyone desires to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.

contextCard.title: Discipleship is movement
contextCard.body: Jesus does not call people only to agree with him intellectually. He calls them to follow him with surrendered lives, changed priorities, and daily obedience.

questions.prompt: What does Jesus promise to make the first disciples as they follow him?
questions.explanation: Jesus says he will make them fishers for men.

questions.prompt: Following Jesus in Luke 9:23 includes denying yourself and taking up your cross.
questions.explanation: Jesus connects discipleship with self-denial and daily cross-bearing.

questions.prompt: Which response best reflects Jesus' call to follow him?
options: Keep Jesus as a private interest while changing nothing
Delay obedience until life becomes easier
Reorder your life around obedience to Jesus
Follow only when it costs nothing
questions.explanation: Following Jesus means real obedience, not casual admiration.

reflection.prompt: What current priority would have to move if you took Jesus' call to follow him more seriously?

mission.intro: The path forward is discipleship, not spectatorship.
mission.victoryText: You answered the call to follow, not merely to observe.

units.title: Love Your Enemies
units.summary: Jesus commands a kingdom-shaped love that reaches even enemies and persecutors.

passages.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you.
But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.

focus.statement: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.

contextCard.title: Kingdom love is different
contextCard.body: Jesus teaches a kind of love that does not depend on how others treat us. His disciples are called to reflect the mercy of the Father, not the hostility of the world.

questions.prompt: What response does Jesus command toward enemies?
options: Love them and pray for them
questions.explanation: Jesus commands active love, prayer, and good toward enemies.

questions.prompt: Jesus teaches that loving only those who love you is enough.
questions.explanation: Jesus says even sinners do that. His disciples are called beyond that standard.

questions.prompt: Love your enemies and _____ for those who persecute you.
questions.explanation: Prayer is part of Jesus' command.

reflection.prompt: Where is Jesus calling you to reject revenge and choose mercy instead?

mission.intro: Kingdom victory does not come through retaliation.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by answering with mercy, not revenge.

units.title: Seek First the Kingdom of God
units.summary: Jesus teaches his followers to put God's kingdom and righteousness ahead of anxious pursuit of material security.

passages.text: But seek first God's Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

focus.statement: Seek first God's Kingdom, and his righteousness.

contextCard.title: A reordered life
contextCard.body: Jesus is not teaching passivity. He is teaching priority. The disciple's life is not to be driven first by anxious scrambling, but by the kingdom of God.

questions.prompt: What does Jesus tell his disciples to seek first?
questions.explanation: Jesus directs his followers to seek God's kingdom and righteousness first.

questions.prompt: Jesus' teaching in Matthew 6 is closely connected to anxiety and trust.
questions.explanation: The passage addresses worry and redirects attention to kingdom priorities.

questions.prompt: Which response best matches this teaching?
options: Pursue God's kingdom before lesser concerns
questions.explanation: Jesus calls for kingdom-first living, not anxious or careless living.

reflection.prompt: What concern most often competes with seeking God's kingdom first in your life?

mission.intro: The disciple chooses kingdom priority over anxious distraction.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by choosing the kingdom over fear.

units.title: Forgive Others
units.summary: Jesus teaches that forgiven people must become forgiving people.

passages.text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you. But if you don't forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don't each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.

contextCard.title: Forgiveness is not optional
contextCard.body: Jesus treats forgiveness as a necessary fruit of grace received. The disciple is not free to hold onto bitterness while asking God for mercy.

questions.prompt: According to Jesus, what should characterize a disciple's response to others' sins?
questions.explanation: Jesus calls for real forgiveness from the heart.

questions.prompt: Jesus treats forgiveness as a minor issue with little spiritual importance.
questions.explanation: Jesus treats forgiveness as deeply serious.

questions.prompt: Forgive your brother from your _____.
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes heart-level forgiveness.

reflection.prompt: Is there a person or wound where Jesus is confronting your refusal to forgive?

mission.intro: Unforgiveness hardens the heart and clouds the way forward.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by choosing mercy over bitterness.

units.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
units.summary: Jesus invites persistent prayer and promises that the Father responds generously to his children.

passages.text: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.

focus.statement: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.

contextCard.title: Prayer shaped by trust
contextCard.body: Jesus does not teach prayer as empty words. He teaches confidence in the Father's goodness and persistence in seeking him.

questions.prompt: Which three verbs does Jesus use to teach prayer persistence?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches prayer persistence with the words ask, seek, and knock.

questions.prompt: Jesus presents the Father as reluctant and unwilling to give good gifts.
questions.explanation: Jesus compares the Father favorably even to earthly parents.

questions.prompt: Which response best fits this promise?
options: Stop praying quickly when answers seem delayed
Pray persistently because the Father is good
Treat prayer as unnecessary because God already knows
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches confident persistence, not prayerlessness.

reflection.prompt: Where do you need renewed persistence in prayer rather than quiet resignation?

mission.intro: Locked doors yield to persistent seeking in the presence of a good Father.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by asking, seeking, and knocking in trust.

units.title: Come to Me and I Will Give You Rest
units.summary: Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to him and receive rest for their souls.

passages.text: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.

focus.statement: Come to me... and I will give you rest.

contextCard.title: Rest found in Jesus
contextCard.body: Jesus does not invite the strong to self-sufficiency. He invites the weary to himself. His yoke is not the crushing burden of self-salvation, but the discipleship rest of walking with him.

questions.prompt: Who does Jesus invite in Matthew 11:28?
options: Those who labor and are heavily burdened
questions.explanation: Jesus invites the weary and burdened.

questions.prompt: Jesus promises rest for the soul, not deeper exhaustion.
questions.explanation: Jesus says, "I will give you rest."

questions.prompt: Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you _____.
questions.explanation: Jesus promises rest.

reflection.prompt: Where are you carrying burdens that you have not actually brought to Jesus?

mission.intro: The exhausted traveler presses on only by coming to Jesus.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by receiving the rest Jesus offers.

units.title: Abide in Me
units.summary: Jesus teaches that fruitfulness comes from remaining in him rather than trying to live spiritually independent lives.

passages.text: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can't bear fruit by itself, unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.

contextCard.title: Fruit comes from union
contextCard.body: Jesus does not present discipleship as independent effort. The branch lives by remaining connected to the vine. Fruit is the result of abiding, not mere self-generated activity.

questions.prompt: According to John 15, why can't a branch bear fruit by itself?
options: It must remain in the vine
questions.explanation: Fruit depends on remaining in the vine.

questions.prompt: Jesus teaches that spiritual fruitfulness can come apart from remaining in him.
questions.explanation: He says, "Apart from me you can do nothing."

questions.prompt: Which response best reflects abiding in Jesus?
options: Treat spiritual growth as self-powered achievement
Remain dependent on Jesus for lasting fruit
questions.explanation: Abiding means dependence, not self-sufficiency.

reflection.prompt: Where are you trying to produce fruit without remaining close to Jesus?

mission.intro: Only a branch joined to the vine can endure and bear fruit.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by remaining in the vine rather than trusting yourself.

units.title: Do Not Be Afraid
units.summary: Jesus repeatedly calls his followers away from fear by anchoring them in his presence and authority.

passages.text: But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Cheer up! I AM! Don't be afraid."
Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you. Not as the world gives, give I to you. Don't let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

contextCard.title: Peace in his presence
contextCard.body: Jesus does not deny danger, but he meets fear with his presence, peace, and authority. Courage in the disciple is not self-confidence, but confidence in Christ.

questions.prompt: What does Jesus tell his disciples in the storm?
options: Cheer up and don't be afraid
questions.explanation: Jesus speaks courage into their fear.

questions.prompt: Jesus says, "Don't let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful."
questions.explanation: This is part of his peace-giving teaching in John 14.

questions.prompt: Peace I leave with you. My _____ I give to you.
questions.explanation: Jesus gives his peace to his followers.

reflection.prompt: What fear is most often shaping your decisions more than Jesus' presence and peace?

mission.intro: Fear closes the path, but Jesus speaks peace into the storm.
mission.victoryText: You advanced by trusting his presence more than your fear.

units.title: Make Disciples of All Nations
units.summary: Jesus sends his followers to make disciples by going, baptizing, and teaching obedience to all he commanded.

passages.text: Go, and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you.

contextCard.title: The Great Commission is a teaching commission
contextCard.body: Jesus does not command mere information transfer or crowd gathering. He commands disciple-making that includes teaching people to obey all that he commanded.

questions.prompt: According to Matthew 28, what are disciples to be taught?
questions.explanation: Jesus says to teach them to observe all he commanded.

questions.prompt: The Great Commission includes teaching obedience, not only baptism.
questions.explanation: Jesus explicitly includes teaching obedience.

questions.prompt: Which response best reflects the Great Commission?
options: Make disciples by teaching obedience to Jesus
Treat Jesus' commands as optional extras
Reduce mission to private belief alone
questions.explanation: Disciple-making includes teaching people to obey Jesus.

reflection.prompt: How could your life become more aligned with Jesus' command to make disciples rather than only consume teaching?

mission.intro: This mission is larger than survival. It is about obedience to the risen King.
mission.victoryText: You advanced under the authority of the One who sends disciples to all nations.
